newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - US T-bonds testing key retracement levels.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - US T-bonds testing key retracement levels.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures, which have reversed down sharply after months of a strong bull run, are testing key retracement levels that could determine the market's medium-term resilience, technical analysts said.
September T-bond futures fell more than a point on Friday to to a low of 112-27/32 in mid-morning .

Scott Siller, a senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch, said 113-4/32 was the 38-percent retracement of the last upward leg from the June 30 low to the August 1 high, and the next target would be 112-24/32, the 38-percent retracement of the whole April-August rally.
The 112-24/32 is also the June 20 high, one of the three major peaks during the April-August uptrend, he added.
"So, that looks like a nice place to go to," he said.

Siller noted that the down move from last Friday's 116-31/32 high had so far looked corrective but the medium-term outlook was beginning to look soft after the steep trendline for the rally was broken.
He added that daily oscillators had been showing strong bearish divergence prior to the downturn and were now taking their toll.
Furthermore, the dollar's uptrend against the mark and the yen has also been bent this week, while commodity prices were starting to bounce.
Thus, bounces near-term would likely be lame unless they came at significant price levels or were very strong, Siller predicted.

"Daily studies are oversold and we could get a reaction higher, but that may only be corrective," Siller said. He added that a move back above 115-1/2 would be needed to repair the damage and keep the uptrend intact.

Michael Zentz, Treasury market strategist at FX Concepts, said the mid-112-area could be the next level for the market to stabilize. That level was the measured target for the second mini-wave of the down move from the 116-31/32 high.

Earlier in the day when the initial slide paused, Zentz saw possibilities of some pre-weekend short-covering that could induce follow-through buying early next week. But the renewed mid-morning slide wiped out that chance.
"I wouldn't think about possibilities of a decent rebound again until the mid-112-area," he said.

He noted that there was a big gap on the daytime-only chart between today's pit-session high of 113-27/32 and Thursday's 114-5/32 pit-session low. The market had a chance to fill that gap, but a move away from it was markedly bearish, he said.
"If we start breaking down, then I would have to assume that gap's sort of a measure of strength for the downtrend," Zentz said.
